chunks: Ayyūb ibn al-Ḥurr narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh, from his father, peace be upon them both, who said:
There is no harm in the payment of the wailing woman who mourns over the deceased, and the payment of the singer who escorts brides; there is no harm in it, and she is not one upon whom men enter.

key_terms.أَجْرِ: payment or wage received for a service
key_terms.النَّائِحَةِ: a woman who wails or mourns the deceased
key_terms.تَزُفُّ: escorts or leads in bridal procession

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to take payment for mourning the dead or singing at wedding processions in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the permissibility of taking payment for certain forms of women's work, including mourning for the deceased and singing in the context of escorting brides. It also places a condition on the latter, indicating permissibility where she is not in a setting of improper interaction with men.
